Each time a structure level is actually computed (not answered by the administrator bypass, the availability check, or the permissions cache), usage statistics are counted through the plugin's statistics manager, when exactly one is enabled: for a structure with at least one `PermissionRule.ApplyStructure` rule the counter `calcPermissionWithApplyRule` is incremented and the level is computed a second time ignoring the structure's own top-level apply rules; if that gives a different level, `calcPermissionWithApplyRuleThatMatters` and `calcPermissionWithApplyRuleThatMatters.<actual level>.<level without apply>` (enum constant names, e.g. `calcPermissionWithApplyRuleThatMatters.EDIT.VIEW`) are incremented and the user is recorded under `usersAffectedByApplyRule`. For a structure without apply rules `calcPermissionWithoutApplyRule` is incremented. Counting never changes the returned level; statistics stay local (SPEC.md 1.8).

A computed structure level is remembered per (structure ID, user key) and returned for later requests with the same pair without computing again. Anonymous and a user whose key is null share the key "". The key does not include the structure's contents, so a structure object with changed rules but the same ID gets the remembered level until the cache is cleared. Asked about no structure (null), it answers `PermissionLevel.NONE` without caching.

All remembered answers (levels, app-permission answers, administrator answers, 'may create issues' answers, single-viewable-structure answers) are dropped together on the first access that comes more than 5 minutes (by `System.nanoTime()`) after the previous drop; the very first access after start also drops (empty) caches and starts the 5-minute period. So changes made outside the plugin (Jira groups, project roles, administrator rights, configuration) can take up to 5 minutes to show.

Clearing the permission caches (what `structure-manager` does when a structure is created, saved or deleted) drops every remembered answer on this node at once, restarts the 5-minute period, and then sends the cluster message `clearPermissionCaches` to the other nodes; a node receiving that message drops its caches the same way. A failure to send the message is logged and not thrown; the local clear has already happened.

Answers for the nine `CoreAppPermissions` (computed as in the `permissions-calculator` claims) are remembered per permission and user key; the first answer for a pair is reused until the next drop. A `StructureAppPermission` that is not one of the nine throws `IllegalArgumentException` with message `Unknown permission: <permission>`.

The Jira-administrator answer and the 'may create issues in an enabled project' answer are also remembered per user key until the next drop. The cached administrator and plugin-availability answers are the ones used when computing structure and view levels, so a level computed later in the same period uses the remembered answers.
The single-viewable-structure answer is remembered per user key; a remembered 0 (or negative) is returned as null ('no single structure'), a positive value as that structure ID.
View levels are not remembered: each request computes the level again from the view's owner and rules (only the administrator and plugin-availability answers come from the caches).

As a `CachingComponent`: `clearCaches()` drops every remembered answer on this node only, without restarting the 5-minute period and without a cluster message; `clearUserCaches(user)` and `clearUserCaches(userKey)` drop all remembered structure levels (of every user) and, for that user key only, the app-permission, administrator, 'may create issues' and single-viewable-structure answers. A user key that is not a Jira user is handled the same way (no lookup).

The sensitivity policy comes from `StructureConfiguration.getAttributeSensitivitySettings()`: it is read on first use and reused until the component's caches are cleared (`clearCaches()`), which happens on all nodes whenever the settings are saved through `StructureConfiguration.setAttributeSensitivitySettings` (it clears all plugin caches). `clearUserCaches` does nothing.
For an attribute spec the policy gives one of three answers: sensitive; not sensitive by default; not sensitive because the administrator listed it.
`AttributeSensitivityMode.PERMISSIVE`: every attribute is 'not sensitive by default'; the administrator's list is ignored.

`AttributeSensitivityMode.STANDARD`: an attribute matching the administrator's list is 'listed'; otherwise it is 'not sensitive by default' when its value format is `ValueFormat.NUMBER`, `BOOLEAN`, `DURATION` or `TIME`, or its format's value class carries the annotation `NonSensitiveInStandardMode`; every other attribute (for example text, HTML, JSON) is sensitive.
`AttributeSensitivityMode.STRICT`: an attribute matching the administrator's list is 'listed'; every other attribute is sensitive, whatever its format.

An attribute spec matches the administrator's list when it equals a listed spec, or when a listed spec has the same ID and the same value format (a listed spec with format `ValueFormat.ANY` matches any format) and every parameter of the listed spec is present in the attribute's parameters with an equal value (the attribute may have more parameters). Example: listed `{id: customfield, params: {fieldId: 10001}}` with format any matches `customfield` with `fieldId` 10001 in number or text format, but not `fieldId` 10002.

For a list of issues and a user, the role check asks Jira once, `ProjectRoleManager.createProjectIdToProjectRolesMap(user, <distinct project IDs of the issues>)`, and then answers (issue ID, role ID) without further Jira calls: a null role ID (no role restriction) is always allowed; an issue ID not in the list is not allowed; otherwise allowed exactly when the user holds that role in the issue's project according to that one answer.
Building the role check fails when the issue list contains two issues with the same ID (`IllegalStateException` for the duplicate key) or a null entry (`NullPointerException`).

The group check asks Jira once for `GroupManager.getGroupNamesForUser(user)` and then answers a group name without further calls: null (no group restriction) is always allowed, otherwise allowed exactly when the name is among the returned names (case-sensitive comparison). A null user throws `NullPointerException` when the check is built.

These checks are what the comment and worklog attributes use to hide comments and worklogs whose visibility is restricted to a project role or group the user does not have; the answers are fixed when the check is built, so later membership changes are not seen by it.

A stored permission scheme spec (as used by notes) is decoded by trying, in order: a JSON object with a `structure` parameter that reads as a long (a structure-bound scheme); one of the exact lower-case words `none`, `view`, `edit`, `admin` (a fixed level); the exact text `defaultNote` (the default-note scheme). Anything else, such as `View`, `{}` or `{"structure":"x"}`, throws `IllegalArgumentException` with message `Cannot parse permission scheme spec: <spec>` (also logged as a warning).

Specs are written as: structure-bound `{"structure":<id>}`; fixed level the lower-case level name (`none`, `view`, `edit`, `admin`); default note `defaultNote`. Two schemes are equal when they are of the same kind and have the same structure ID or level.
Scheme levels are none < view < edit < admin; a granted level includes every lower one.

In a structure-bound scheme a user's scheme level follows their level on that structure (`StructureManager.getStructurePermission(id, user)`): `ADMIN` gives admin, `EDIT` or `AUTOMATE` gives edit, `VIEW` gives view, `NONE` gives no level at all, so a user without access to the structure (or when it does not exist) is refused even the 'none' level.

A structure-bound refusal carries the reason `Need "<level>" access level to structure <structure>` (`s.permission-scheme.structure.no-permission`), with level text None, View, Edit or Control, and structure text `"<name> (id: <id>)"` when the current `StructureAuth` user can view the structure, else just the ID. Texts are in the language of the current user at the time the spec was decoded.
A fixed-level scheme grants exactly the levels up to its own to everybody, the anonymous user included; a refusal has no reason text.
The `defaultNote` scheme grants view (and none) to everybody and refuses edit and admin with the reason 'Cannot edit default note' (`s.w.notes.note.edit-denied.default`).

Checking a spec for the current user (view, edit, admin, or a given level): true without decoding when `StructureAuth` security is overridden; false when the spec cannot be decoded; otherwise the scheme's answer for the current `StructureAuth` user.
An issue identity whose numeric id is between 1 and 2147483647 maps to that id as its code, without storing anything; mapping it again always gives the same code.

Any other identity (non-issue items, and issues with an id of 0, negative or above 2147483647) gets a negative code assigned on first request: -1, then -2, -3, ... in request order. The same identity (by equals) always gets the same code for the life of the node; the mapping is in memory only and starts again from -1 after a restart.
Decoding gives null for 0, the issue identity with that id for a positive code, the identity assigned to a negative code, and null for a negative code never assigned.
Mapping a null identity throws IllegalArgumentException `itemId must not be null`. Mapping and decoding are safe for concurrent use (one lock guards the assigned codes).

Each transient row created gets the next odd id 1, 3, 5, ... (the n-th row since start gets 2n-1), held in memory only; numbering starts again at 1 after a restart. The row keeps its item identity, semantics, creator id and original id. This is the store behind the transient rows of `structure-row-manager`.

Semantics, creator id and original id are kept as 32-bit values: a value outside the int range is logged as an error and kept as 0. Reading a row returns a TransientRow with the stored creator and original ids.

Reading a row by id throws MissingRowException for an id that is not transient (0, negative or even) and for a transient id that was never created (or was lost on restart); otherwise it returns the row with its item resolved lazily by `item-resolver` per the access mode.

Scanning a list of ids visits them in the given order and stops as soon as the predicate returns false. An id that is not transient throws IllegalArgumentException `<id> is not a transient row id`. A transient id with no row goes to the missing collector, or throws MissingRowException when no collector is given.
Finding rows of an item reports the ids of all its transient rows, newest first, until the consumer returns false (the search then reports that it was stopped); a null item reports nothing.

Finding rows of an item made by one creator reports only the rows with that creator id, newest first, stopping when the consumer returns false. The per-creator index behind it is cached and dropped after 60 s (dark feature `structure.ftrm.cache.timeout`; concurrency `structure.ftrm.cache.concurrency`) and rebuilt from all rows of the creator on the next use, with the same results. If loading the index fails, a warning is logged and nothing is reported.

Transient rows are never deleted one by one, also not when their creator generator is gone: they live until restart. The only removal drops all transient rows at once, either keeping the numbering (the next id continues) or resetting it so the next row is 1 again; nothing in the plugin triggers that removal on Jira 9.12.

On start it registers usage statistics with `statistics-manager`: `transientTotalRowCount` (number of transient rows) together with `transientTotalRowCount.<bin>` where bin is the first of 1000, 10000, 30000, 50000, 70000, 100000, 200000, 300000, 400000, 500000, 1000000, 2000000, 5000000 not below the count, or `inf`; and `transientRowsItemCreatorCacheMissToTotal` = index rebuilds / index lookups, left out while no lookup happened.

Item identities of transient rows are encoded through `item-identity-mapper`; if a stored code can no longer be decoded, the row counts as missing (MissingRowException with message `cannot unmap item identity from idx <code>, row <id> cannot be used`, or the id goes to the missing collector with a warning).

Each HTTP session id has its own clipboard forest, kept in memory on the node: the first request for a session creates an empty clipboard, later requests return the same one. Clipboards are never shared between sessions and are lost on restart.

Adding (pasting) a fragment into a clipboard first empties it (except on a dry run), then puts the fragment at the top level whatever under/after/before were given. Each row becomes a new transient row (creator 0, original 0) with the same item and semantics, and the action result maps each old row id to its new id; with parameter `reuseRows` true and no id shared with the clipboard's rows, the fragment's row ids are kept. A dry run (`dryRun` true) changes nothing.

Removing from a clipboard is accepted only when the given row ids are exactly its top-level rows in their order, and then removes everything; any other row list fails with StructureException UNSUPPORTED_FOREST_SOURCE_OPERATION. Move and copy actions on a clipboard always fail with UNSUPPORTED_FOREST_SOURCE_OPERATION.

A clipboard's forest version has a random signature chosen when the clipboard is created and a counter starting at 0 that grows by the number of forest changes of each edit. An update request from the current version gets an empty incremental update; from a version at most 2 changes back an incremental update; from anything older or another signature a full update.

Clipboards not requested for more than 30 minutes (dark feature `almworks.attributes.dev.clipboard.timeout`, milliseconds; negative counts as 0) are emptied and dropped. The sweep runs when some clipboard is requested, at most once per minute, before the requested one is looked up; a later request for a dropped session gets a new empty clipboard with a new signature.

Clearing one session's clipboard removes all its rows and returns the forest update since the version before clearing; it returns null when the session has no clipboard. The clipboard itself stays. REST uses this after rows were moved through the clipboard (`viaClipboard`).
A backup restore empties and drops every clipboard of the node.

It defines these field value types, by key: `single-user`, `single-date`, `single-duration`, `single-line-text`, `multi-line-text`, `single-project`, `single-version`, `single-issue-type`, `single-priority`, `single-date-time`, `single-number`, `multi-label`, `multi-version`, `multi-component`, `single-sprint` (only when the agile sprint services are available), `multi-user`, `single-group`, `multi-group`, `single-option`, `multi-option`. There is no resolution type. The catalogue is built once on first use and not refreshed.

Jira custom field type keys map to types: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:` `userpicker` single-user, `datepicker` single-date, `textfield` single-line-text, `textarea` multi-line-text, `project` single-project, `version` single-version, `float` single-number, `datetime` single-date-time, `labels` multi-label, `multiversion` multi-version, `multiuserpicker` multi-user, `grouppicker` single-group, `multigrouppicker` multi-group, `select` single-option, `multiselect` multi-option; `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-sprint` single-sprint (only when that type exists). Every other key has no type.

Each type writes and reads the per-field string stored in a generic item's `fields` map exactly as SPEC's AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM.C_PARAMETERS notes describe (user key, `yyyy-MM-dd`, milliseconds, JSON lists, project id as a floating number, and so on). A null value stores nothing; a stored string that cannot be read back (or names a missing user, version, option, ...) reads as null and is logged as a warning, never thrown.

User input is parsed per type: null gives null; texts treat `` as null; dates use Jira's date-picker format (blank gives null), falling back to ISO `yyyy-MM-dd`; durations use Jira's duration format (for example `2h 30m`, blank gives null) and give milliseconds; date-times fall back to ISO local date-time in the logged-in user's time zone; numbers, priorities and issue types by Jira id; single user, project, version, group, option and sprint values by id. When an input fails the editor form and a second accepted form exists, that one is tried before reporting an error.

An invalid duration reports `createissue.error.original.estimate.invalid` for `timeoriginalestimate`, `createissue.error.remaining.estimate.invalid` for `timeestimate`, `s.column.editor.timespent.error` for `timespent`, and Jira's parse error text for other duration fields.

For single-valued option-backed types (user, project, issue type, priority, version, group, option, sprint) a text input not found as an id is looked up by name. For multi-valued ones (versions, components, users, groups, options), when no element could be read and the input is text, it is split on commas, each part trimmed and looked up by id then name; unknown parts and duplicates (same id) are dropped and an empty result is null. Label lists drop nulls and duplicates, keeping order.

Validating a value against a field configuration fails with `s.ext.type.memo.error.invisible-field` (field name) when the configuration hides the field, and with `s.ext.type.memo.error.required-field` (field name) when the value is empty (null, empty text or empty list) and the field is required. An empty label list validates to null.

For option-backed single values, a value that is not a valid option of the field's option source (per the configuration's option-source spec, for the current StructureAuth user) fails with `s.ext.type.memo.error.misconfigured-field` (field name, value's display text). For multi values, invalid elements fail with the same key listing their display texts, but the failure still carries the valid elements (or null when none), so a read keeps the valid ones; with no invalid element the valid list is returned (null when empty).

Display text: users by display name, dates in Jira's date-picker format, durations in the plugin's duration format, priorities and issue types by their translated name in the user's language, sprints and groups by name; other values through `value-text-converter`.

HTML views: single-line text is HTML-encoded; multi-line text is rendered as wiki markup when the field's renderer is `atlassian-wiki-renderer`, else as text with `
` line breaks; durations as formatted text and sprints and groups as encoded names (empty string for null); labels, components, priority and issue type through Jira's velocity templates (`templates/plugins/fields/view/view-label.vm`, `templates/jira/issue/field/components-columnview.vm`, `.../priority-columnview.vm`, `.../issuetype-columnview.vm`); custom-field-backed types through their Jira type's `column-view` template, or `view` when it has none.

Values given to formulas: a date becomes the epoch milliseconds of the start of that day in the formula's time zone (time format); a date-time its epoch milliseconds; a duration its milliseconds (duration format); a number the number; users, projects, issue types, priorities, versions, components, groups, options, sprints and labels become item identities (lists for multi-valued types); texts stay text. Null stays null.

For backups, option-backed values are exported as a map from stored value to the option's name (looked up without a user, ignoring restrictions), and on restore are found again by name; a name not found fails with `s.ext.type.memo.error.misconfigured-field` (field name and the name, or the stored value). For multi values the found ones are kept and the missing names listed in the error. Other types export and resolve nothing.

The catalogue starts with these Jira system fields in this order, each with its type: `summary` (single-line text, renderer `jira-text-renderer`), `description` (multi-line text, `atlassian-wiki-renderer`), `assignee` (user), `duedate` (date), `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate`, `timespent` (duration), `environment` (multi-line text, `atlassian-wiki-renderer`), `reporter` (user), `priority`, `issuetype`, `project`, `labels` (labels), `versions`, `fixVersions` (multi-version, frother-control renderer), `components` (multi-component, frother-control renderer). A field whose type is missing is left out.

After the system fields come Jira's custom fields (in CustomFieldManager order) whose type key maps to a type of `structure-field-type-manager`; others are left out. A custom field's renderer type comes from its item in Jira's default field layout, when there is one.

A system field's id is its Jira field id and also its plain name; its localized name is the Jira field's name key translated in the requested locale. A custom field's id is `customfield_<n>`, its plain name the untranslated name, and its localized name Jira's translation for the locale, or the untranslated name when there is none.
Looking up a field by id returns the catalogue entry or null for an id not in it (an unsupported custom field, or an unknown id).

The catalogue is reloaded from Jira at most 60 s after it was built (a tuning setting in seconds; its key is not contract), so new or removed custom fields show within a minute; clearing the plugin's caches reloads it at the next use; clearing one user's caches does nothing. A failure to build it surfaces as StructureRuntimeException.

The fixed system fields (summary, description, assignee, due date, estimates, time spent, environment, reporter, priority, issue type, project, labels, affects and fix versions, components) are also available directly, built once and not refreshed; they are used by memos, planning tasks, groupers and effectors.

For memos the field configuration shows and allows editing exactly `summary`, `description`, `assignee`, `duedate`, `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate` and `timespent`, requires none, and asks no Jira configuration.

Under the memo (and migration) configuration, an option-backed field's options come from the type's option source with no project and no filters, except `FIELD_OPTIONS` which gets `customField` = the field id; fields without options have none.
For a planning task the configuration is that of `jira-field-visibility-service` for the task's stored project and issue type (read without validation) and the current StructureAuth user.

Planning-task option sources: field `project` uses PROJECTS with `checkStructureConfig`, `checkCreateIssues`, `excludeInactive`; field `assignee` uses USERS with `excludeInactive`, `checkAssignable` and the task's project; otherwise by source PROJECTS (`checkStructureConfig`, `excludeInactive`), VERSIONS, COMPONENTS, USERS, SPRINTS (`excludeInactive`), ISSUE_TYPES (`excludeSubtasks`), FIELD_OPTIONS (`customField`, `excludeInactive`, and `issueTypeId` when known). The task's project id is passed for ISSUE_TYPES, PRIORITIES, VERSIONS, COMPONENTS, FIELD_OPTIONS, SPRINTS and assignee only. When the project is not visible to the user, every option-backed field gets the empty source `EMPTY`.

Applying field updates checks each one: a field the configuration does not let edit fails with `s.ext.type.memo.error.uneditable-field` (field name in the user's language); otherwise the type's validation applies (see `structure-field-type-manager`). Each failure is reported for its field and that field is not written; valid ones are written in SPEC's stored format: summary to the item name, description to the item description, others into the `fields` map (null removes the key, an empty map removes `fields`, and the estimate fill-in applies).

When an item is created, every catalogue field except `summary` that the configuration requires and that is neither being set nor already stored is checked as if set to null, so a missing required field fails (with `s.ext.type.memo.error.required-field`, or `uneditable-field` when the user may not edit it).

A planning task is visible to a user only when its stored project is visible to that user per `jira-field-visibility-service` (no project means not visible); memos are always visible by this check (structure ownership is checked elsewhere).

For backup restore, a planning task needs its project key and issue type name: no key fails with `s.ext.type.memo.error.project-required`, an unknown key with `s.ext.type.memo.error.project-not-found` (key); no issue type name with `s.ext.type.memo.error.issue-type-required`, a name matching no Jira issue type exactly with `s.ext.type.memo.error.issue-type-not-found` (name). Otherwise, and for memos, the configuration lets every field be shown and edited and requires none.
For planning tasks, `project` and `issuetype` are always visible and required, even when the project or issue type is unknown.
`timespent` is never visible, required or editable for planning tasks; `timeoriginalestimate` and `timeestimate` are checked as Jira's `timetracking` field.

Any other field is visible only when both the project and the issue type are known, Jira's field layout for that project and issue type has the field and does not hide it, and the field is on the create-issue screen (any tab) of the project's issue type screen scheme for that issue type; a custom field on that screen counts only when it is in scope for the project and issue type. Without a screen scheme or create screen nothing else is visible.

A visible field is required when its field layout item is required, it has no default value, and it is on the create screen. Defaults: reporter and priority always have one; assignee has one unless the project's default assignee is the project lead (assignee type 2) and the lead is missing or not assignable (ASSIGNABLE_USER); description and custom fields have one when the field configuration for the project and issue type gives a non-empty default value.

A visible field is editable when: `assignee` and the user has ASSIGN_ISSUES on the project; `reporter` and MODIFY_REPORTER; `duedate` and SCHEDULE_ISSUES; a custom field that Jira marks not editable never; the agile sprint field with SCHEDULE_ISSUES; anything else always. Permissions are checked for the user on the project as for issue creation; without a project they fail.

A project is visible to a user when it is a valid option of the PROJECTS option source with `checkStructureConfig`, `checkCreateIssues` and `excludeInactive` for that user (anonymous when the user is null); a null project is never visible.

Answers are cached per (project id, issue type id, user key) and dropped 60 s after they were computed (dark feature `FieldConfigService.refreshTimeout`, seconds); the per-user project option source expires 1 hour after its last use (dark feature `FieldConfigService.projectVisibilityLifespan`, hours). Clearing the plugin's caches drops both; clearing one user's caches drops only that user's entries. A failure to compute them surfaces as an unchecked exception.

The key of a memo is `MEMO:<id>`, of a planning task `PT:<id>`, of any other item null. The board link of a generic item is `<base URL>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<owning structure id>#layout=details&itemId=<HTML-encoded item identity>`.
For formulas, a memo or planning task gives: `key` its key; `name` and `summary` the item name; `description` the description (undefined/null when absent).

Formula field `history` gives the list of the item's history records as items `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo-change-history-group/<record id>` (from `generic-item-history-manager`); `created` the time of its create record and `updated` the latest record time (epoch ms); `creator` the user item of the create record's author (null when none). For many items at once only `history` is loaded in bulk.

Any other formula field name is turned into a field id (`affectedversions` -> `versions`, `fixversions` and also `versions` -> `fixVersions`, `attachments` -> `attachment`, `originalestimate` -> `timeoriginalestimate`, `remainingestimate` -> `timeestimate`) and looked up in `structure-field-manager`; if not found, a field whose name matches after removing whitespace, punctuation and control characters and lower-casing is used; none gives undefined. The value is read with validation (invalid reads as null) and given in its formula form (see `structure-field-type-manager`).

When a memo or planning task is created or edited from client values, `description` is taken from the values and the field values from the `params` map (field id to editor value); only fields known to `structure-field-manager` that the configuration shows and lets edit are used, others are ignored. Each is parsed as user input; a parse error is recorded under the field id in the user's language.

On edit, any parse error means nothing is applied. On create, all values are applied and all errors collected, and required fields not given are checked too. Validation errors (see `generic-item-field-config-service`) are added under the field id unless that field already has an error. The remaining `params` are then passed on to the item type (for example a memo's colour and icon).

A field view of an item identity loads the item through GenericItemManager.getItem (its cache; no permission or app-access check) and gives nothing when the item does not exist; its configuration comes from `generic-item-field-config-service` for the item's type and the current user. For a list of identities it keeps the order and leaves out missing items.

Reading a field reads the stored string (summary from the name, description from the description, others from `fields`), converts it with the field type and validates it with the configuration: a failure reads as null, except for multi-valued option-backed fields (versions, components, users, groups, options) where the valid elements are kept and only invalid ones dropped.
The fields of a view are the catalogue fields whose ids are keys of the item's `fields` map; keys unknown to `structure-field-manager` are skipped.

Reading or setting a custom field through the typed accessors throws IllegalArgumentException `Field <field name> is unsupported` when `structure-field-manager` does not know it and `Field <field name> is of wrong type` when its type does not match the accessor (text accepts single- and multi-line text).

An update builder records field values for one identity (the last value per field wins) and stores them as `memo-manager` and `planning-task-manager` describe: it reads the item through GenericItemService as the current user, applies and validates the recorded values (failure: StructureException UPDATE_ITEM_FAILED with the field's localized message), then runs GenericItemService.validateUpdate and update and throws their exception, or UPDATE_ITEM_FAILED with the joined error messages when there is none.

The same builder can only validate: it gives the first problem as a localized text (field error, or the item service's error) or null when the update would pass, and stores nothing; `memo-field-effect-provider` uses this before applying a change.

When a backup is restored, a generic item's `fields` map is rebuilt only from the restored field values, validated with the migration configuration; a failing field throws StructureException UPDATE_ITEM_FAILED for that item with the field's message. Other parameters (such as a memo's colour) are kept.

Converting an issue to planning-task field values always starts with the issue's project and issue type, and uses the planning-task configuration of that project and issue type for the current StructureAuth user.

It then takes every other field of `structure-field-manager` (in catalogue order) that this configuration shows, is not excluded by the caller and exists as a Jira field: the issue's value is read and converted to the field's value with `field-information-provider`; fields it has no conversion for, and empty results, are skipped. Hidden fields (for example `timespent`, or fields not on the create screen) are never copied.

Copying into a planning task validates and writes these values like any field update (see `generic-item-field-config-service`): fields the user may not edit or whose value is invalid there are not copied and get a localized error under their field id in the caller's error collection; the others are written.
When a planning task is created with an issue as its sample, the issue's values are copied this way with `summary` excluded (the summary is given separately).

Module `type-structure` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Structure`, no children) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-structure`. Items are long identities whose number is the structure id (the `ID` of AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE).

An identity resolves to the structure with that id, looked up through `StructureManager.getStructure(id, PermissionLevel.VIEW)` with security overridden (so it resolves for every caller, also anonymous). A structure that does not exist (or any `StructureException` from the lookup) gives no object. The type does not check that the identity's type key is its own; the number is used as is.
A structure item is visible to a user (null = anonymous) exactly when that user's level on the structure (`StructureManager.getStructurePermission(id, user)`) includes `PermissionLevel.VIEW`.

In a bulk access check the type looks at the long ids of this key only and, with the `StructureAuth` context switched to the given user and security-override flag, reports as inaccessible every structure id for which `StructureManager.isAccessible(id, PermissionLevel.VIEW)` is false: structures that do not exist, and (unless security is overridden) structures the user may not view. With no structure ids it does nothing.

The structure item type reports no dead items, exposes no formula fields and no display text of its own (formulas show the simplified identity text, e.g. `structure/12`), and cannot be created, copied into a structure or edited through the item type. Changes of these items are recorded by `structure-manager` when the structure changes.

Module `type-issue` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Issue`, no children) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`. Items are long identities whose number is the Jira issue id (a bare decimal in item id text, see `ItemIdentity`).

A long identity of this key resolves to Jira's `IssueManager.getIssueObject(id)` (null when the issue does not exist). The placeholder `CoreIdentities.NEW_ISSUE` (id Long.MAX_VALUE) and identities of other types resolve to nothing. Resolving many issues at once asks `IssueManager.getIssueObjects(ids)` once for all issue identities in the batch (others are skipped) and reports each issue found under its own issue identity; ids not found are not reported.

An issue is visible to a user (null = anonymous) when Jira's `PermissionManager.hasPermission(ProjectPermissions.BROWSE_PROJECTS, issue, user)` is true (this includes issue security levels as Jira applies them).

In a bulk access check the issue ids of this key are judged as `forest-permissions-cache` does for `collectInvisibleIssues` (with the given user and security-override flag), and each issue id it reports is collected as an inaccessible issue identity. Before that, the placeholder id Long.MAX_VALUE (`NEW_ISSUE`) is removed from the id set taken from the input, so the placeholder is never reported; this removal changes the caller's input set in place (as the original does).
An issue id of this key is reported dead when `IssueManager.getIssueObject(id)` returns null.

The issue item type records nothing itself; changes of issue items reach the item tracker through `data-tracker` (every issue in an event of the issue event bridge) and through `structure-event-bridge` (single archived issues, Tempo Planner allocations).

For formulas (`issue.<field>`, name lower-cased) an issue gives (here and for all item types, a true/false field is the number 1 or 0, a date is a number of epoch milliseconds, and a null value is undefined): `key` the issue key; `issubtask` whether it is a sub-task; `votes` and `watches` the counts; `created`, `updated`, `resolutiondate` those timestamps; `url` the Jira base URL + `/browse/` + key; `subtasks` an array of the sub-task issue items; `parent` the parent issue item (undefined for a non-sub-task); `history` an array of the issue's change history group items (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-change-history-group`), from Jira's `ChangeHistoryManager.getChangeHistories(issue)`; `remotelinks` an array of its remote link items (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-remote-link`), from `RemoteIssueLinkManager.getRemoteIssueLinksForIssue`.

Any other field name of an issue is mapped first (`affectedversions` to Jira field `versions`; `fixversions` and also `versions` to `fixVersions`; `attachments` to `attachment`; `originalestimate` to `timeoriginalestimate`; `remainingestimate` to `timeestimate`; otherwise the name itself) and looked up as a field known to `field-information-provider`; when it is not one, it is resolved as a custom field name in the issue's context by `custom-field-resolver` and read as `customfield_<id>`; an unknown name gives undefined. The value is the field's value as `field-information-provider` reads and formats it for the formula's time zone. When that gives nothing for a custom field, the raw value from the custom field type is used instead, turned into text by `value-text-converter` (a collection becomes an array of texts, null elements dropped). So `issue.versions` gives the fix versions, not the affected versions.

When the `history` field is needed for many issues at once, all their change groups are read in one database query (Jira entity `ChangeGroup` with `issue` in the issue ids), and each issue gets the change history group items of its rows; issues without history get nothing. For other fields there is no bulk read.
The display text of an issue item is its issue key; issues are ordered by that key as plain text (so `ABC-10` sorts before `ABC-9`).

Creating an issue (`/item/create` with this type) reads these values: `sampleItemId` (item id text of an existing issue to copy from), `pid` (project id), `issuetype` (issue type id), `mode` (`clone`, ignoring case, means clone mode; any other text means no clone; when absent, clone mode is on exactly when a sample is given), `parentIssue` (parent issue id for sub-tasks) and `issue` (a map of Jira field ids to values). Single values follow `StructureUtil.getSingleParameter`/`getSingleParameterLong` (a missing or unparsable number counts as 0).

Creation fails with `StructureException` `INVALID_PARAMETER` (nothing created), checked in this order: `sampleItemId` that does not parse: `Cannot parse sample item Id (<text>)`; one that is not an issue: `Cannot create an issue from something that is not an issue (<text>)`; no sample and not both a positive `pid` and an `issuetype`: `Cannot create issue without sample issue or project/type pair`; clone mode without sample: `Cannot clone without sample`; a blank or missing `summary` in `issue`: `Cannot create issue without summary`. A non-map `issue` counts as no field values.

Each entry of the `issue` map becomes a Jira action parameter: null gives an empty value list, a scalar gives its `String.valueOf`, an array or collection gives the texts of its elements. A value that is a map fails with `INVALID_PARAMETER` `Value cannot be object`; an array element that is null, an array, a collection or a map fails with `INVALID_PARAMETER` `Value array cannot contain null, array or object`. The same conversion is used for the values of an issue update.

The issue is created as Jira's logged-in user (`JiraAuthenticationContext`). A sample must exist and be browsable by that user, else `INVALID_PARAMETER` `Issue <sampleId> is not found or not accessible`. The project is `pid` when positive, otherwise the sample's project; none: `INVALID_PARAMETER` `Project <pid>(<sampleId>) is not found or not accessible`. The issue type is `issuetype` when non-empty, otherwise the sample's type; none: `INVALID_PARAMETER` `Issue type <issuetype>(<sampleId>) is not found`. For a sub-task type the parent is `parentIssue` when positive, otherwise the sample's parent, and must exist and be browsable, else `INVALID_PARAMETER` `Parent issue <parentIssue>(<sampleId>) is not found or not accessible`. No further permission is checked by the plugin; Jira's create validation checks the rest.

In clone mode the new issue takes from the sample: assignee, environment, priority, security level, the sample's non-archived affected versions and fix versions, its components, and the values of every custom field that is required on the create screen of the target project and issue type; the reporter is the creating user, the resolution is empty and the screen check is skipped. In every mode Jira defaults apply to fields not given, the `issue` values are applied on top, and the project and issue type are set as resolved.

When Jira Software is present and the issue type is its epic issue type, an empty or missing Epic Name field value (by the field's id) is filled with the summary. Without Jira Software (no epic type or Epic Name field) nothing is added.

The issue is validated with Jira's `IssueService.validateSubTaskCreate(user, parentId, params)` for a sub-task type, otherwise `validateCreate(user, params)`, and then created with `IssueService.create`. When validation or creation is not valid, Jira's errors are added to the error collection and no identity is returned. After creating a sub-task it is linked to the parent with `SubTaskManager.createSubTaskIssueLink`; a failure to link is only logged. The result is the long identity of the new issue.

The preview row for a new issue goes through the same parameter reading, checks and Jira create validation, but creates nothing: it is a row with the given row id and semantics whose item is `CoreIdentities.NEW_ISSUE`, carrying the issue object of Jira's validation result; when validation fails it is null and Jira's errors are in the error collection.

Editing an issue item fails with `StructureException` `INVALID_PARAMETER` `<item id text> is not an issue ID` for another type and `<item id text> is not a long ID` for a string identity. Then the issue is checked for the `StructureAuth` user as `StructurePluginHelper.getIssueError(issue, true)` does (existence, browse, edit); a problem is thrown as that error for the item with message `Cannot edit issue #<id>`.

The values are converted as for creation and passed to Jira's `IssueService.validateUpdate` and `update` as the `StructureAuth` user, keeping existing values of fields not given. When `timetracking_originalestimate` or `timetracking_remainingestimate` is given, a `timetracking` parameter is added if missing, and when only one of the two is given the other is filled with the issue's current display value of that estimate. Invalid validation or update adds Jira's errors to the error collection and stops (no transition).

When the values contain `status`, after a successful field update the issue is moved to the status with the first given id: an empty list throws `INVALID_PARAMETER` `status value is not defined` (the fields stay updated). Jira's update validation with no values must pass first (its errors are reported). Then exactly one workflow transition must lead from the current status to the target (step actions of the current step and global actions whose result is the target step), else an error message is added in the current user's language: `s.ext.gen.grouper.issuefield.block.status.no-workflow` (`No workflow for {0}.`), `...null-source-status` (`Unknown status of {0}.`), `...null-target-status` (`Unknown target status for {0}.`), `...no-source-status` (`Initial status {0} is not part of the workflow for {1}.`), `...no-target-status` (`Target status {0} is not part of the workflow for {1}.`), `...no-transition` (`Transition from {0} to {1} is not allowed by the workflow for {2}.`), `...many-transitions` (`There are several transitions that can bring {0} from {1} to {2}: {3}. Please use issue actions menu to apply a transition.`, names joined by `, `) or, for a transition with a screen, `...requires-view` (`Transitioning {2} from {0} to {1} requires a dialog to be displayed. Please use "{3}" transition in the issue actions menu.`). The transition is validated and run with `IssueService.validateTransition`/`transition`; its errors are added.

After a successful update (and transition), when the values contain the Jira Software Epic Link field id or a STAGIL Assets relation field (as `stagil-integration` decides), an `IssueChangeEvent` of type `JiraChangeType.ISSUE_UPDATED` for the issue is reported to the issue event bridge, so dependants see the change. Without Jira Software or STAGIL nothing extra is reported.

Module `type-project` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Project`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-project`. Items are long identities whose number is the Jira project id; only identities that are project identities resolve, through `ProjectManager.getProjectObj(id)` (null when no such project).

A project is visible to a user (null = anonymous) when `PermissionManager.hasPermission(ProjectPermissions.BROWSE_PROJECTS, project, user)` is true. In a bulk check the project ids of this key are judged as `StructurePluginHelper.filterInvisibleProjects` does (with the given user and override flag) and each reported id is collected as inaccessible.

A project id of this key is reported dead when `ProjectManager.getProjectObj(id)` returns null. Project changes are recorded by `structure-event-bridge` (project events; deleting or archiving a project resets the tracker).

For formulas a project gives `name`, `key`, `url`, `email` and `description` as text (undefined when null), `lead` the project lead as a user item (undefined when there is no lead); any other field is undefined. Its display text is the project name, and projects are ordered by name as plain text. Projects cannot be created or edited through the item type.

Module `type-version` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Version`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-version`. Items are long identities whose number is the Jira version id; only version identities resolve, through `VersionManager.getVersion(id)` (null when none).
A version is visible to a user when the user has Browse Projects (`ProjectPermissions.BROWSE_PROJECTS`) on the version's project.

In a bulk check every version id of this key that `VersionManager.getVersion` cannot find is inaccessible; the projects of the found versions are judged together as `StructurePluginHelper.filterInvisibleProjects` does (given user and override flag), and every version of a reported project is inaccessible. A found version with no project id is treated as accessible.
A version id of this key is reported dead when `VersionManager.getVersion(id)` returns null. Version changes are recorded by `structure-event-bridge` (the version and its name, old and new).

For formulas a version gives `project` (the project item), `name`, `description`, `isarchived`, `isreleased`, and `releasedate` / `startdate` (undefined when not set); other fields are undefined. A date is converted to the calendar day it falls on in the JVM default time zone, given as the epoch milliseconds of the start of that day in the formula's time zone.

A version's display text is its name; versions are ordered by their Jira sequence number (a version without sequence gets the empty order key). Versions cannot be created or edited through the item type.

Module `type-version-name` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Version Name`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-version-name`. Items are string identities whose id is a version name (as `CoreIdentities.versionName` builds them); any string id of this key resolves to a value carrying that name, without asking Jira whether such a version exists. Long identities resolve to nothing.

A version name item is visible to everyone, including anonymous; the bulk access check reports nothing (not even names no version has), and no dead items are reported. The type exposes no formula fields or display text of its own and cannot be created or edited. Changes are recorded by `structure-event-bridge` (the old and new names of a changed version).

Module `type-label` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Label`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-label`. Items are string identities whose id is the label text. A string id of this key resolves to a Jira `Label` with that text (no id, no issue) when it is not empty, is a valid label for Jira's `LabelParser.isValidLabelName` (for example no spaces) and has at most 255 characters; otherwise, and for long identities, it resolves to nothing. Jira is not asked whether any issue has the label.

A label is visible to everyone; the bulk access check reports nothing and no dead items are reported. Every formula field of a label is undefined; its display text is the label text and labels are ordered by it as plain text. Labels cannot be created or edited through the item type, and no label changes are recorded.

Module `type-loop-marker` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Loop Marker`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-loop-marker`. Items are long identities whose number is the row id of the row whose item would repeat (the loop target). Any identity resolves to itself (the identity object), whether or not the row exists.
A loop marker is visible to everyone; the bulk access check reports nothing. It exposes no formula fields or display text, and cannot be created or edited. No changes are recorded for loop markers.

A loop marker is reported dead when its target row id is negative (a temporary row) or odd and positive (a transient row), or when it is even and positive and the row manager (`RowManager.getRow`) throws `MissingRowException` for it. A target id of 0 is not reported. Every identity in the given set is examined; with assertions enabled (as the tests run) an identity that is not a loop marker throws `AssertionError`, with them disabled it is judged by its number the same way.

Module `type-generator` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Generator`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-generator`. Items are long identities whose number is the public generator id: `AO_8BAD1B_GENERATOR.C_ID * 2` for stored generators (even), odd numbers for transient ones (as `generator-manager` issues them).

A generator identity (other than `CoreIdentities.NEW_GENERATOR`) resolves to the generator configured with the stored module key and parameters, as one of inserter, extender, grouper, filter or sorter. It resolves to nothing when there is no such generator, the module is not installed or failed to load, the module fails, or the module is none of those kinds; such failures are only logged at debug level.

A generator item is visible to everyone; the bulk access check reports nothing, and no dead items are reported. It exposes no formula fields or display text. Generator changes are recorded by `generator-manager` on update and delete.

Creating a generator reads the values as exactly two keys: `moduleKey` (text, the complete generator module key) and `params` (a JSON object of the generator's parameters). When the values are empty, contain any other key, have values of the wrong shape, or `moduleKey` is missing or blank, the field error `moduleKey` with text `s.ext.it.generator.error.module-blank` (`Module key is required`) is added and nothing is created.

`createItem` stores a new generator through `generator-manager` with the given module key and parameters and no owning structure, and returns its long identity (the public id). It does not check that the module is installed.

The preview row of a new generator resolves the module with the parameters: an uninstalled module throws `StructureException` `UNAVAILABLE_MODULE` (`Generator module <key> is not found` or `... failed to resolve`). A module that is none of inserter, extender, grouper, filter or sorter gives null without errors. Otherwise the row has the given row id and semantics and the item `CoreIdentities.NEW_GENERATOR`.

When a stored generator (positive even id with a row) is placed into structure S: if it has no owning structure it is updated in place to be owned by S (same identity, same key and parameters); if it is owned by another structure, or by S when a copy is asked for even for the same owner, a new stored generator with the same module key and parameters owned by S is created and its identity is used instead. Transient or temporary ids, missing generators and other identities are returned unchanged.

Module `type-user` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:User`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-user`. Items are string identities whose id is the Jira user key (`-` for the anonymous user, see `CoreIdentities.user`). A string id of this key resolves to `UserManager.getUserByKey(key)` (null when none); long identities resolve to nothing.
A user item is visible to everyone, including anonymous; the bulk access check reports nothing.

A non-empty user key of this type is reported dead when `UserManager.getUserByKey` finds no user; this includes the anonymous id `-` when no user has that key. User changes are recorded by `structure-users-event-bridge`.

For formulas a user gives `key`, `name` (user name), `isactive`, `emailaddress` and `displayname`; other fields are undefined. The display text of a user item is its user key (not the display name), and users are ordered by key as plain text. Users cannot be created or edited through the item type.

Module `type-folder` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Folder`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-folder`. A long identity's number is the `ID` of AO_8BAD1B_FOLDER and resolves to the stored folder from `folder-manager` (null when none; `CoreIdentities.NEW_FOLDER` resolves to nothing). A string identity is a virtual folder whose name is the string id (for example the group folders of groupers); it always resolves, to an unstored folder with that name and no owning structure.
Folders are visible to everyone; the bulk access check reports nothing. Folder changes are recorded by `folder-manager` on create and update.
A long folder id is reported dead when `folder-manager` has no folder with that id; string (virtual) folders are never dead.

For formulas a folder gives `name`; other fields are undefined. The display text is the folder name (for a virtual folder the raw string id, not translated), and folders are ordered by name as plain text.

Creating a folder uses the single value `summary` as its name (not trimmed). A missing or blank name adds the field error `summary` with text `s.ext.it.folder.error.name-blank` (`Folder name is required`) and nothing is created. `createItem` stores a folder with that name and no owning structure through `folder-manager` and returns its long identity; the preview row has the given row id and semantics, the item `CoreIdentities.NEW_FOLDER` and a folder with that name.

Renaming a folder throws `StructureException`: `INVALID_PARAMETER` `<item id text> is not a folder ID` for another type and `<item id text> cannot be edited` for a string (virtual) folder; `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` for the item (`folder <item id text> is not found or not accessible`) when no such folder is stored, or when its owning structure is not accessible at `PermissionLevel.VIEW` for the `StructureAuth` user (a folder without owner always fails here); `ITEM_EDIT_DENIED` with localized message `s.item.edit.error.no-edit-perm` (`No "Edit" permission for structure {0}.`, the structure id) when the user can view but not edit the owning structure.

After the checks, the single value `summary` becomes the folder's new name (owner unchanged) through `folder-manager`; a missing or blank value adds the field error `summary` `Folder name is required` and changes nothing.

When a stored folder is placed into structure S: a folder without owner becomes owned by S in place (same identity); a folder owned by another structure, or by S when a copy is asked for even for the same owner, is copied into a new stored folder with the same name owned by S, and the new identity is used. String (virtual) folders, missing folders and other identities are returned unchanged.

Module `type-status` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Status`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-status`. Items are string identities whose id is the Jira constant id (for example `10001`); a string id of this key resolves to `ConstantsManager.getStatus(id)` (null when none), and long identities resolve to nothing.
These items are visible to everyone, including anonymous; the bulk access check reports nothing. A string id of this key is reported dead when Jira finds no constant with that id.

For formulas the item gives `name`, `description` and `sequence` (the Jira sequence number); other fields are undefined. Statuses also give `category`, the primary alias of the status category (Jira `StatusCategory.getPrimaryAlias()`, for example `To Do`). The display text is the name.

Module `type-resolution` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Resolution`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-resolution`. Items are string identities whose id is the Jira constant id (for example `10001`); a string id of this key resolves to `ConstantsManager.getResolution(id)` (null when none), and long identities resolve to nothing.
These items are visible to everyone, including anonymous; the bulk access check reports nothing. A string id of this key is reported dead when Jira finds no constant with that id.
For formulas the item gives `name`, `description` and `sequence` (the Jira sequence number); other fields are undefined. The display text is the name.

Module `type-issuetype` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Issue Type`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issuetype`. Items are string identities whose id is the Jira constant id (for example `10001`); a string id of this key resolves to `ConstantsManager.getIssueType(id)` (null when none), and long identities resolve to nothing.
These items are visible to everyone, including anonymous; the bulk access check reports nothing. A string id of this key is reported dead when Jira finds no constant with that id.

For formulas the item gives `name`, `description` and `sequence` (the Jira sequence number); other fields are undefined. Issue types also give `issubtask`, whether it is a sub-task type. The display text is the name.

Module `type-priority` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Priority`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-priority`. Items are string identities whose id is the Jira constant id (for example `10001`); a string id of this key resolves to `ConstantsManager.getPriorityObject(id)` (null when none), and long identities resolve to nothing.
These items are visible to everyone, including anonymous; the bulk access check reports nothing. A string id of this key is reported dead when Jira finds no constant with that id.
For formulas the item gives `name`, `description` and `sequence` (the Jira sequence number); other fields are undefined. The display text is the name.
Statuses are ordered by their Jira sequence number (none gives the empty order key). Statuses cannot be created or edited through the item type, and no status changes are recorded.
Resolutions are ordered by their Jira sequence number (none gives the empty order key). They cannot be created or edited through the item type, and no resolution changes are recorded.

Issue types are ordered by their Jira sequence number (none gives the empty order key). They cannot be created or edited through the item type; issue type events are recorded as changes by `structure-event-bridge`.

Priorities are ordered by the negated Jira sequence number (sequence 1 gets order key -1, sequence 5 gets -5, so in ascending order the highest sequence number comes first). When the dark feature `structure.expr.priority.straightOrder` is true (read once when the type is created, default false) the sequence number itself is used. A priority without sequence gets the empty order key. Priorities cannot be created or edited; edited and deleted priorities are recorded as changes by `structure-event-bridge`.

Module `type-group` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Group`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-group`. Items are string identities whose id is the Jira group name; a string id of this key resolves to `GroupManager.getGroup(name)` (null when none), long identities to nothing.

A group is visible to everyone; the bulk access check reports nothing and no dead items are reported. For formulas a group gives `name`, other fields undefined; its display text is the group name and groups are ordered by it as plain text. Groups cannot be created or edited; membership changes are recorded by `structure-users-event-bridge`.

Module `type-cf-option` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Option`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-cf-option`. Items are long identities whose number is the Jira custom field option id; a long id of this key resolves to `OptionsManager.findByOptionId(id)` (null when none), string identities to nothing.
Options are visible to everyone; the bulk access check reports nothing. An option id of this key is reported dead when `OptionsManager.findByOptionId` finds none. No option changes are recorded.

For formulas an option gives `value` (its text), `isdisabled`, `sequence` and `parent` (the parent option item for a cascading child, undefined for a top-level option); other fields are undefined. Options are ordered by their display text as plain text. Options cannot be created or edited through the item type.

The display text of a top-level option is its value; for a child option it is the values from the top-most ancestor down to the option joined with ` - ` (for example `Europe - France`), following at most 10 parent levels above the option.

Module `type-sprint` (element `structure-item-type`, name `itemtype:Sprint`) defines the item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-sprint`. Items are long identities whose number is the Jira Software sprint id; a long id of this key resolves to the sprint read without a user through `gh-integration` (by id from Jira Software's sprint manager). Without Jira Software, or when the sprint does not exist, it resolves to nothing; string identities resolve to nothing.

A sprint is visible to a user when Jira Software's `SprintService.getSprint(user, id)`, asked through `gh-integration`, returns the sprint for that user (null user = anonymous); when it gives nothing the sprint is invisible. The type has no bulk access check (each item is checked on its own) and reports no dead items.

For formulas a sprint gives `name`, `goal`, `state` (`ACTIVE`, `FUTURE` or `CLOSED`), `sequence`, `startdate`, `enddate` and `completedate` (epoch milliseconds, undefined when not set) and `originboardid` / `rapidviewid` (both the sprint's board id); other fields are undefined. Its display text is the sprint name; sprints are ordered by sequence.
Sprints cannot be created or edited through the item type. Sprint changes are recorded by `structure-event-bridge` (Jira Software sprint events).

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-tempo-account` (descriptor name `itemtype:Account`). Items are long identities whose number is the Tempo account id; an identity is resolved only when it is a long identity of exactly this key, and the number is narrowed to a 32-bit int (higher bits dropped) before the account is asked of `tempo-integration` by id. Any other identity resolves to nothing.

An item resolves to the Tempo account (id, key, name, status) that `tempo-integration` returns for the id. When that is the null account (id -1: Tempo Accounts not installed or disabled, no such account, or any Tempo failure), the item resolves to nothing.

A resolved Tempo account is visible to every user, including anonymous; no Jira or Tempo permission is asked. The type takes part in bulk access checks but never reports any item as inaccessible (not even accounts that do not exist), and it does not report dead items.

Tempo account items expose no formula fields and no display text of their own through the type, cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type, and the plugin records no item changes for Tempo accounts (no Tempo account event is turned into a change of this item type).

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-project-component` (descriptor name `itemtype:Project Component`). Items are long identities whose number is the Jira project component id; only long identities of this key are resolved, through Jira's `ProjectComponentManager.find(id)`. An `EntityNotFoundException` from Jira gives nothing.

A component is visible to a user when Jira's `PermissionManager.hasPermission(BROWSE_PROJECTS, project, user)` is true for the component's project (looked up with `ProjectManager.getProjectObj(projectId)`); a null user is asked as anonymous.

In a bulk access check, every component id of this type that Jira cannot find is reported inaccessible. The projects of the found components are checked together as `StructurePluginHelper.filterInvisibleProjects` does (with the given user and security-override flag), and every component whose project is reported there is inaccessible. A found component whose project id is null is never reported.
A component id of this type is reported dead when Jira's `ProjectComponentManager.find` throws `EntityNotFoundException` for it; found components are alive.

Formula fields of a component: `name` its name, `description` its description, `lead` the user item (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-user`/<lead user key>) of its lead, undefined when it has no lead. Null name or description, and any other field name, give undefined. Its display text is its name.

Changes of a component (any Jira project component event: created, updated, deleted, merged) are recorded as changes of its item by `structure-event-bridge`; the item type itself records nothing. Components cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-missing` (descriptor name `itemtype:Missing Item`), used for rows whose item cannot be resolved; its identities (for example `CoreIdentities.MISSING_ITEM`, long id 0) may be long or string.
Every identity given to this type resolves to nothing, and its visibility check answers false for any user.

In bulk checks every identity of type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-missing` in the set (long and string ids alike) is reported inaccessible, even when security is overridden, and also reported dead. Identities of other types are not touched. No formula fields, no creation or editing, no change tracking.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-sd-request-type` (descriptor name `itemtype:Customer Request Type`). Items are long identities whose number is the Service Management request type id (an int widened to long). The identity's number is converted to an int; a number outside the 32-bit range is logged as an error and 0 is used instead. The type key of the identity is not checked, and a string identity throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (which `item-resolver` logs and turns into no item).

An item resolves to the Service Management `RequestType` that `sd-integration-supplier` loads by id as the current Structure user (first result of the request type query). When Service Management is not installed or its request type service is unavailable, or nothing is found, the item resolves to nothing.

A request type is visible to a user only when Service Management (`com.atlassian.servicedesk`) is installed and ENABLED and the request type can be loaded by its id with that user as the requesting user (a non-null result); otherwise it is invisible. The type has no bulk access or dead-item checks.

Formula fields of a request type: `name` its name, `issuetype` the issue type item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issuetype`/<issue type id as decimal text> (a string identity), `description` its description, `helptext` its help text; null texts and any other field name give undefined. Its display text is its name.
Request types cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type, and the plugin records no item changes for request types.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector` (descriptor name `itemtype:Effector`). Items are long identities whose number is the `AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_INSTANCE.ID` of an effector instance. Long identities of this key other than `CoreIdentities.NEW_EFFECTOR` (id Long.MAX_VALUE) resolve to the `EffectorInstance` that `effector-instance-manager` returns; `NEW_EFFECTOR`, other types and string identities resolve to nothing, and a `StructureException` from the manager is logged at debug level and gives nothing.
An effector instance is visible to every user, including anonymous, and the bulk access check never reports any effector item as inaccessible (also not for ids with no instance).

Creating an effector item takes a values map that is read as exactly two keys: `moduleKey` (the effector module's complete key, text) and `params` (a JSON object of effector parameters). When the map is null or empty, when it cannot be converted (any other key, or values of the wrong shape, are rejected by the conversion, logged as a warning), or when `moduleKey` is missing or blank, an error is added under field `moduleKey` with the text of `s.ext.it.effector.error.module-blank` (`Module key is required`) and nothing is created (null is returned). The module key is not checked against installed effectors.

With valid values, creating an item creates an unowned effector instance through `effector-instance-manager` (module key and params as given, owning structure null) and returns `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector`/<new instance id>. No permission is checked.

A preview (dummy) row for a new effector is built from the same values with the same `moduleKey` validation and error, without storing anything: the row has the given row id and semantics, item `CoreIdentities.NEW_EFFECTOR`, and as its item object an `EffectorInstance` with id 0, the given module key, no owning structure and the given params (an empty map when `params` is absent).

When an effector item is placed into structure S (as `StructureOwnedItemType`): an instance with no owning structure is updated in place to be owned by S (module key and parameters unchanged) and its identity is returned; an instance owned by another structure, or owned by S when copying is requested (copy-if-same), is copied into a new instance owned by S with the same module key and parameters and the new identity is returned; an instance already owned by S without copy-if-same is returned unchanged. The identity's type key is not checked.
When the effector instance of the identity does not exist, placing it into a structure fails with the `StructureException` of `effector-instance-manager` (`ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`).

Effector items have no formula fields or display text through the item type and cannot be edited through it (no update support). Their changes are recorded by `effector-instance-manager` when instances are created, updated or deleted.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo` (descriptor name `itemtype:Memo`), a generic item type behaving as `GenericItemType` describes, with long ids = `AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM.ID`. Its descriptor has `<icon spanClass="alm alm-fw alm-memo s-item-color-gray"/>`, `<displayable key="s.ext.type.memo.displayable"/>` (`memo "{0}"`) and `<title key="s.ext.type.memo.title"/>` (`Memo`).

A memo is visible exactly as `generic-item-manager` decides for generic items: always when it has no owning structure, otherwise when the user has at least VIEW on the owning structure. No Jira permission and no field configuration is consulted.

When a memo is created or edited from client values, the fields are read under the memo field configuration (`generic-item-field-config-service`: summary, description, assignee, due date and the three time fields) as `generic-item-type-helper` reads them: `description` and the entries of `params` that are known, shown and editable fields. On create all errors are collected; on edit any field parse error means no field is applied.

Besides fields, of the `params` map only `color` and `iconClass` are stored, each only when the key is present (its value stored as given under the same key in the item's parameters; a null value removes it). Other non-field entries of `params` are not stored.

Formula field `color` of a memo gives the stored `color` parameter as a formula value (undefined when absent); every other field (`key`, `name`, `summary`, `description`, `history`, `created`, `updated`, `creator` and catalogue fields) is answered as `generic-item-type-helper` describes, including its bulk loading of `history`. A memo's display text is its name.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task` (descriptor name `itemtype:PlanningTask`), a generic item type behaving as `GenericItemType` describes, with long ids = `AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM.ID`. Its descriptor has `<icon spanClass="alm alm-fw alm-issue-icon"/>`, `<displayable key="s.ext.type.planning.displayable"/>` (`Planning task "{0}"`) and `<title key="s.ext.type.planning.title"/>` (`Planning task`).

A planning task is visible to a user only when both hold: the generic item rule of `generic-item-manager` (no owning structure, or VIEW on it) and the planning-task field configuration rule of `generic-item-field-config-service` (its stored project is visible to the user). The same rule is used in bulk access checks, so a task without a project is inaccessible unless security is overridden.

When a planning task is created or edited from client values (without a sample), the field configuration used is the planning-task configuration for a project and issue type taken from `params.project` and `params.issuetype` (parsed as editor values of those fields), each falling back to the value already in the item being built when not given or not parseable to a value. The fields are then read as `generic-item-type-helper` reads them (create collects all errors, edit applies nothing on a parse error); no other `params` entries (for example colour or icon) are stored.

Values may contain `sampleItemId`, an item identity in text form (`<item type>/<id>`). When it is present, all other values except the name (`summary`) are ignored. A text that cannot be parsed adds the error message `Invalid sample item id format: <parse error>`; an identity that is neither an issue (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`) nor a planning task adds `Sample item is not supported` (both plain English, not translated); nothing is copied then.

A planning-task sample is resolved with the visibility check for the current user; when found, the new item gets the sample's description and its whole parameter map (all field values and other parameters), replacing what was there. When it does not resolve, the error message `s.planning-task.error.sample-not-found` (`Sample item does not exist`) is added.

An issue sample is resolved with the visibility check for the current user; when found, its values are copied into the planning task by `issue-to-planning-task-converter` with `summary` excluded (the name comes from `summary` in the values). When the issue does not resolve, `s.planning-task.error.sample-not-found` (`Sample item does not exist`) is added.

`sampleItemId` is honoured on edit as well as on create: editing a planning task with a sample overwrites its description and parameters (planning-task sample) or copies the issue's values into it (issue sample).

For showing the fields of a not-yet-created planning task (REST field accessor), the type builds an unsaved item from client values: name = the single value of `summary` (empty text when absent, no blank check), field configuration from `params.project`/`params.issuetype` as on create, and the fields read with all errors collected; `sampleItemId` is not honoured here and nothing is stored.

Every formula field of a planning task (`key`, `name`, `summary`, `description`, `history`, `created`, `updated`, `creator` and catalogue fields) is answered as `generic-item-type-helper` describes, including its bulk loading of `history`; there is no `color` field of its own. Its display text is its name.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-attachment` (descriptor name `itemtype:Attachment`). Items are long identities whose number is the Jira attachment id; long identities of this key resolve to Jira's `AttachmentManager.getAttachment(id)` (an exception from Jira, such as for a missing attachment, is logged by `item-resolver` and gives nothing); other identities resolve to nothing.

An attachment is visible to a user when Jira's `PermissionManager.hasPermission(BROWSE_PROJECTS, issue, user)` is true for the attachment's issue (so issue security applies as Jira applies it). There are no bulk access or dead-item checks.

Formula fields of an attachment: `created` its creation time (epoch ms), `filesize` its size in bytes, `filename` its file name, `author` the user item of its author key (undefined when the author key is null); null values and other field names give undefined. Its display text is the file name.
Attachments cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type, and the plugin records no item changes of this type.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-comment` (descriptor name `itemtype:Comment`). Items are long identities whose number is the Jira comment id; long identities of this key resolve to Jira's `CommentManager.getCommentById(id)` (null when missing); other identities resolve to nothing.

A comment is visible to a user when Jira's `PermissionManager.hasPermission(BROWSE_PROJECTS, issue, user)` is true for the comment's issue. The comment's own visibility restriction (group or project role) is not checked. There are no bulk access or dead-item checks.

Formula fields of a comment: `author` and `updateauthor` the user items (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-user`/<user key>) of its author and update author, undefined when Jira has no such user object; `created` and `updated` the times (epoch ms); `body` the body text. Null values and other names give undefined. Its display text is the body.
Comments cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type, and the plugin records no item changes of this type.
