Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-worklog` (descriptor name `itemtype:Worklog`). Items are long identities whose number is the Jira work log id; long identities of this key resolve to Jira's `WorklogManager.getById(id)`; other identities resolve to nothing.

Work logs are resolved in bulk: the distinct ids of work log identities (other identities ignored) are loaded with `WorklogManager.getWorklogsForIds` in one call when there are fewer than 1000, otherwise in chunks of at most 1000 ids; each loaded work log is reported under its own identity, and ids Jira does not return are reported as not found.

A work log is visible to a user when Jira's `PermissionManager.hasPermission(BROWSE_PROJECTS, issue, user)` is true for its issue; the work log's own group or role restriction is not checked. There are no bulk access or dead-item checks.

Formula fields of a work log: `author` and `updateauthor` the user items of the author and update author keys (a null key gives the anonymous user item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-user`/`-`, not undefined); `created`, `updated` and `startdate` times (epoch ms); `comment` the comment text; `timespent` the time spent in milliseconds (Jira's seconds times 1000; undefined when null). Other names give undefined.

A work log's display text is `s.ext.type.worklog.description` (`{0} logged {1}`) in Jira's default locale, with the author's display name and the time spent formatted by Jira's duration format in that locale (`0m` when that gives nothing).
Work logs cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type, and the plugin records no item changes of this type.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue-link` (descriptor name `itemtype:IssueLink`). Items are long identities whose number is the Jira issue link id; long identities of this key resolve to Jira's `IssueLinkManager.getIssueLink(id)`; other identities resolve to nothing.

An issue link is visible to a user only when both its source and destination issues are visible to that user, as `forest-permissions-cache` reports invisible issues (without security override, so cached per user); one invisible or deleted end makes the link invisible. No bulk access or dead-item checks.

Formula fields of an issue link: `source` and `destination` the issue items of its two ends, `sequence` its sequence number, `type` the issue link type item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue-link-type`/<link type id>; other names give undefined. Its display text is `<source issue key> → <destination issue key>` (U+2192 between single spaces).
Issue links cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type, and the plugin records no item changes of this type.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue-link-type` (descriptor name `itemtype:IssueLinkType`). Items are long identities whose number is the Jira issue link type id; long identities of this key resolve to Jira's `IssueLinkTypeManager.getIssueLinkType(id)`; other identities resolve to nothing.
An issue link type is visible to every user, including anonymous. No bulk access or dead-item checks.

Formula fields of an issue link type: `name`, `inward`, `outward` and `style` its texts (undefined when null), `issubtask` true (1) or false (0) for the sub-task link type, `issystem` and also `system` true (1) or false (0) for a system link type; other names give undefined. Its display text is its name.
Issue link types cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type, and the plugin records no item changes of this type.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-change-history-group` (descriptor name `itemtype:ChangeHistoryGroup`). Items are long identities whose number is the id of a Jira change group (one issue change event); long identities of this key resolve to Jira's `ChangeHistoryManager.getChangeHistoryById(id)`; other identities resolve to nothing.

Change groups are resolved in bulk with one query of Jira's `ChangeGroup` entity (via `OfBizDelegator`) for all ids of this type (other identities ignored, id `IN` list); each row found is reported under its own identity, ids without a row are reported as not found.
A change group is visible to every user, including anonymous; the visibility of the changed issue is not checked. No bulk access or dead-item checks.

Formula fields of a change group: `author` the user item of its author key (a null key gives the anonymous user item `-`); `time`, `timeperformed` and `timestamp` the time of the change (epoch ms); `item`, `changeditem`, `issue` and `changedissue` the issue item of the changed issue; `changes` and `changeitems` an array of the group's change items (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-change-history-item`/<ChangeItem id>), read from Jira's `ChangeItem` entity by its `group` column, in the order the database returns them (empty array when none). Other names give undefined.

For many change groups at once only `changes`/`changeitems` is loaded in bulk: one query of `ChangeItem` rows whose `group` is any of the groups' ids, delivering each change item to its group. Other fields are answered per item.

A change group's display text is `s.ext.type.change.group.description` (`Changed on {0}`) in Jira's default locale, with the change time formatted by Jira's date-time formatter in DATE style for that locale.
Change groups cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type, and the plugin records no item changes of this type.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-change-history-item`. Items are long identities whose number is the id of a row of Jira's `ChangeItem` entity (one field change: field name, old value and text, new value and text, group id), read with `OfBizDelegator.findById`. Other identities resolve to nothing; an id with no row fails while reading (a `NullPointerException`, which `item-resolver` logs and turns into no item).

Change items are resolved in bulk with one `ChangeItem` query by id (`IN` the list of ids of this type; others ignored); each row found is reported under its identity, ids without a row are reported as not found.
A change item is visible to every user, including anonymous; the changed issue's visibility is not checked. No bulk access or dead-item checks.

Formula field `field` gives the change's field name, with Jira's history names `Version` turned into `affectedversions`, `Fix Version` into `fixversions` and `Component` into `components`; other names (including custom field names and `Attachment`) unchanged.

Formula fields `fromtext` and `totext` give the old and new display strings of the change (undefined when null); `changegroup` the change group item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-change-history-group`/<group id>. Other unknown names give undefined.

To interpret values the field is looked up in `field-information-provider`: by field id, mapping history names `Version`->`versions`, `Fix Version`->`fixVersions`, `Component`->`components`, `Attachment`->`attachment` (others as is); when that gives nothing, the custom fields with that exact name are taken (Jira `CustomFieldManager.getCustomFieldObjectsByName`) and the one with the lowest id is looked up. The lookup is reused within one formula evaluation context.

Formula fields `from` and `to` give the old and new values: when the field has both history support and value format support, the raw value and text are read as a field value (in the formula's time zone) and formatted as a formula value; a value that cannot be read gives the display string when the field allows fallback, otherwise undefined. For a multi-valued field, elements that read as null are replaced by the matching element of the display string split on `, ` (when fallback is allowed). Without such support the result is the display string, or the raw value when the string is null or empty.

Formula field `incremental` is true (1) when the field's history support marks it incremental (for example multi-value fields whose history records additions and removals), and undefined otherwise (also when the field is unknown).

A change item's display text is `s.ext.type.change.item.description` (`{0} {1} {2}`) in Jira's default locale: the field name as given by `field`, then `-=` with the old text when the new text is empty or null (a removal), else `+=` with the new text for an incremental field, else `→` with the new text.
Change items cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type, and the plugin records no item changes of this type.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo-change-history-group`. Items are long identities whose number is `AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY.ID`, one change record of a memo or planning task. Identities of this type resolve to the record `generic-item-history-manager` returns for them (other identities to nothing); in bulk, records are loaded as that manager's bulk load does and each is reported under `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo-change-history-group`/<record id>.
A generic item history record is visible to every user, including anonymous; the visibility of the changed item or its owning structure is not checked. No bulk access or dead-item checks.

Formula fields of a record: `author` the user item of its author key (null gives the anonymous user item `-`); `time`, `timeperformed` and `timestamp` its time (epoch ms); `item`, `changeditem`, `memo` and `changedmemo` the identity of the changed generic item (memo or planning task); `changes` and `changeitems` the array of its field changes (see the change entries claim). Other names give undefined. There is no bulk field loading.

The changes of a record compare the old and new item snapshots field by field over the union of their field ids: `summary` (the name), `description` (only when not null) and every entry of the item parameters' `fields` map. A field whose old and new values are equal is left out; order of entries is unspecified. Each change is a struct with `fieldid` (field id with whitespace, punctuation and control characters removed, lower-cased), `field` (the field's name from `structure-field-manager`, or the normalised id when unknown), `fromtext` and `totext` (the stored old and new values as stored), `from` and `to` (for `summary`, `description` and unknown fields the stored value; otherwise the stored text deserialised by the field's type and converted to its extended value, a non-text stored value read as null), and `changegroup` (the record's item). For a create record all old values are absent.
A record's display text is `s.ext.type.change.group.description` (`Changed on {0}`) in Jira's default locale, with the record time formatted by the date-time formatter for that locale.
Records cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type; the item type records no item changes (records are only appended by `generic-item-manager`).

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-insight-object`. Items are long identities whose number is the Insight/Assets object id; the number is narrowed to a 32-bit int and the object loaded by id through `insight-integration-supplier`. The identity's type key is not checked; a string identity throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (logged by `item-resolver`, no item).

An item resolves to the Insight object (id, label, object key, object type id). When Insight/Assets is not installed, its object facade is unavailable, the object does not exist, or Insight throws its permission exception, the item resolves to nothing; other Insight exceptions propagate (and `item-resolver` logs them and gives nothing).

An Insight object is visible to a user only when the user is not anonymous and Insight's `InsightPermissionFacade.hasInsightObjectViewPermission(user, objectId)` is true; a missing permission facade (Insight absent) makes it invisible. No bulk access or dead-item checks.

Formula field `label` gives the object's label. Any other field name is normalised (whitespace, punctuation and control characters removed, trimmed, lower-cased) and matched against the object's attributes with their names normalised the same way; the first matching attribute is converted to a formula value by `insight-expr-converter`. No matching attribute (or no attributes, for example Insight absent) gives undefined. The display text is the label.

Changes of an Insight object are recorded as changes of its item by `structure-event-bridge` (Insight object updated events); the item type itself records nothing, and objects cannot be created, copied or edited through it.

Item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-remote-link` (descriptor name `itemtype:RemoteLink`). Items are long identities whose number is the Jira remote issue link id; long identities of this key resolve to Jira's `RemoteIssueLinkManager.getRemoteIssueLink(id)`; other identities resolve to nothing.
A remote link is visible to a user only when its issue is visible to that user, as `forest-permissions-cache` reports invisible issues (without security override). No bulk access or dead-item checks.

Formula fields of a remote link: `source` and `issue` the issue item of its issue; `title`, `url`, `apptype` (application type), `appname` (application name), `icontitle`, `iconurl`, `statusicontitle`, `statusiconurl`, `statusiconlink`, `statusname`, `statusdescription`, `statuscategorykey`, `statuscategorycolor` (status category colour name), `summary` and `relationship` the link's matching texts (undefined when null). Other names give undefined.

A remote link's display text is `<issue key> → <title>`: the issue key from Jira's `IssueManager.getIssueObject(issueId)` (the numeric issue id when the issue is not found) and the title, or the URL when the title is null.
Remote links cannot be created, copied or edited through the item type, and the plugin records no item changes of this type.

The `servlet-filter` `security-filter` (location `before-login`, weight 200, dispatchers `REQUEST`, `INCLUDE`, `FORWARD`, `ERROR`) acts on `/secure/StructureExternalGadget.jspa`, for anonymous and logged-in users alike, and is declared with Atlassian's unrestricted-access annotation so that it is never refused. It sets the page's `Content-Security-Policy` so that the page may be framed by `'self'` and by the applications linked to Jira. Other headers, `X-Frame-Options` included, are not touched by it.

Before the chain it takes the response's current `Content-Security-Policy` (possibly none) and sets the combined policy on the response, so the header is present even when nothing downstream sets one. With no current header the value is `frame-ancestors 'self' <origins>`, or just `frame-ancestors 'self'` with no application links.

The chain receives a response wrapper. A `setHeader` whose name equals `Content-Security-Policy` ignoring case sets the combined policy of the given value instead of the value itself, under the exact name `Content-Security-Policy`. Other `setHeader` calls pass through unchanged. `addHeader` is not intercepted, for this header either, and goes straight to the real response.

When the policy has a directive that starts, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, with `frame-ancestors ` (with the space), the directive is rewritten in place and the directives are joined with `;`: its existing sources come first in their order, then `'self'` and the link origins, without duplicates, separated by one space. Example with one link: `default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors https://a.example` becomes `default-src 'self';frame-ancestors https://a.example 'self' https://b.example`. A trailing `;` is lost and other directives keep their own spacing. Applying the filter again (on a forward) changes nothing, because of the de-duplication.
A `frame-ancestors` directive whose only source is `'none'` (ignoring case) is replaced by `frame-ancestors 'self' <origins>`.

A policy with no such directive gets one appended, with a `;` added first when the trimmed policy does not end with one: `default-src 'self'` becomes `default-src 'self';frame-ancestors 'self' <origins>`. A null, empty or blank policy gives only the directive. A bare `frame-ancestors` with no following space does not count as a directive, so a second one is appended.

The origins are computed from `ReadOnlyApplicationLinkService.getApplicationLinks()`: for each link both `getDisplayUrl()` and `getRpcUrl()` count, reduced to `scheme://host` plus `:port` when a port is given, except that port 443 with `https` and port 80 with `http` are dropped. Path, query and user info are removed, and equal origins appear once. The directive always begins with `'self'`; the order of the origins after it is not defined.

The origins are kept in the Atlassian cache `com.almworks.jira.structure.app-links` (one entry, created by a cache loader on the first request after a clear) and reused for all requests. Any `ApplicationLinkEvent` on Jira's `EventPublisher` clears the cache, so a link change shows on the next request.
The filter registers its listener on `EventPublisher` when created; `destroy()` unregisters it and logs a warning that it is stopping.

When computing or setting the policy before the chain throws an `Exception` (for example when application links cannot be read), it is logged as an error and the chain is never called: the request ends with an empty response (as the original does).

An `Exception` thrown by the chain, `IOException` and `ServletException` included, or by a later policy update, is logged as an error (`Unexpected exception in servlet filter`) and does not propagate, so the container's error handling never sees it (as the original does). An `Error` does propagate.
A request or response that is not HTTP goes down the chain unchanged. An `Exception` from that chain is logged and swallowed too.

The `servlet-filter` `partitioned-cookie-header-filter` (location `after-encoding`, no weight, dispatcher `REQUEST`) is declared on `/secure/StructureExternalGadget.jspa` and `/rest/tsv/1.0/authenticate*`, with Atlassian's unrestricted-access annotation. It acts only on requests with scheme `https` and method `POST`, both compared ignoring case. Anything else, including any request the container reports as `http`, goes down the chain with the original objects.

For an acting request whose URI does not end with `/rest/tsv/1.0/authenticate` (the gadget page login post), the chain gets a response wrapper: when `sendRedirect` is called, the `Set-Cookie` headers are rewritten first and then the redirect goes on to the same location. A response that does not redirect (such as a failed login that shows the form again) keeps its cookies as they were.

For an acting request whose URI ends with `/rest/tsv/1.0/authenticate`, the filter acts only when the request parameter `s_partitioned` is exactly `true` (case-sensitive). Otherwise the original response goes down the chain.

With `s_partitioned=true` the chain gets a response wrapper: on every `setHeader` call, whatever the header, the `Set-Cookie` headers present at that moment are rewritten and then the header is set. `addHeader`, `addCookie` and `sendRedirect` trigger nothing, so cookies added after the last `setHeader` stay as they are. A `setHeader` of `Set-Cookie` itself stores its value unmodified.

Rewriting appends to each target cookie's header, in this order, `; Secure`, `; SameSite=None` and `; Partitioned`. Each attribute is skipped when its name (`Secure`, `SameSite`, `Partitioned`) already occurs anywhere in that header text, compared case-sensitively, so an existing `SameSite=Lax` stays Lax and a lower-case `secure` gets a second `Secure`. All else in the header is kept, and rewriting twice changes nothing.

The target cookies are `JSESSIONID`, `INGRESSCOOKIE` and the names in dark feature `structure.partitioned.cookies.additional`, a comma-separated list read at each rewrite; names are trimmed, empty ones skipped, and matched case-sensitively against the cookie name. Other cookies keep their header text unchanged.
A rewrite replaces all the `Set-Cookie` headers: the first usable one with `setHeader`, the others with `addHeader`, in the original order. Blank headers are skipped.

A `Set-Cookie` header that `java.net.HttpCookie.parse` rejects (a warning is logged) or that parses into other than one cookie is not written back, so it disappears from the response when any other usable `Set-Cookie` header exists (as the original does). When no usable header exists, nothing is rewritten and all headers stay.
The filter catches nothing: an exception from the chain, or from a rewrite, reaches the caller. It has no effect on the page's content and does not change the request.

The plugin descriptor has exactly one `ao` element, with key `ao` and namespace `com.almworks.jira.structure`. That namespace is what makes Active Objects use the table prefix `AO_8BAD1B_` (the last six hex digits of the namespace's MD5, `7f218d86d83be3046b5516c4528bad1b`, upper-cased), so with the same namespace a replacement sees the tables the original left in the database, and with any other it sees none of them.

The `ao` element lists 39 `entity` children, one for each table in SPEC §1.5 and no more: reading the descriptor and each entity's explicit table name gives exactly those 39 names, each entity with its own table, and nothing else. No entity relies on Active Objects deriving a table name from the entity's class name, so renaming an entity type does not move its table.

The `ao` element has only `entity` children: it declares no Active Objects upgrade task, so the module writes no model version of its own. On plugin start, Active Objects only compares the declared entities with the database: a missing table or column is created, and rows the original wrote are left in place. The module itself runs no data migration.

The module's whole job is to declare the schema: it does no reads or writes of its own. All access to these tables goes through the modules that use Active Objects (`ao-helper`, `structure-database-provider`, `ao-initializer` and the stores built on them), and it is those modules' claims that say when tables are first used and what happens before Active Objects is ready.
